# The local stack, measured

The full environment is 10 containers: redis, mailpit and the collector from
`docker-compose.yml`, and seven Supabase containers (db, kong, auth, rest, storage,
studio, pg_meta).

Resident memory totals about 805 MiB against the VM's 3.815 GiB, the largest single
container being storage at 242 MiB. The 2 CPU and 4 GiB VM holds it with room, which
settles the observation the clarify record left open.

That is with `analytics`, `realtime` and `edge_runtime` disabled in
`supabase/config.toml`. Analytics alone is Logflare plus a second Postgres, and it is
why the default stack does not fit comfortably on a small VM. Nothing in the product
reads any of the three: traces go to the collector, no subscription reads Postgres
changes, and nothing runs on Deno.

Timing: `supabase start` took 49s on a machine holding none of its images, and 24s
warm. The three compose services were healthy within 6s.

## Two obstacles the next machine will also meet

The colima profile carried `disk: 20` against an instance already grown to 100 GiB,
and the daemon refused to start at all until `~/.colima/_lima/colima/colima.yaml`
matched the instance. Neither `colima start --disk 100` nor editing
`~/.colima/default/colima.yaml` reaches that file.

Studio refuses to start unless `supabase/snippets` exists beforehand: docker chowns a
mount source path it creates itself, and colima's virtiofs denies the chown. Creating
the directory first is enough, so `dev:up` creates it.
